goal: Derive OOOI (Out/Off/On/In) events and periodic enroute position reports from existing flight-state and track data in src/flightManager.ts, and file them as downlink/uplink ACARS messages in the already-shipped acars_messages substrate (src/db/acarsMessages.ts, src/acars.ts), reusing insertAcarsMessageOnce + dedup keys so a repeated frame or transition can never double-file, and adding no new position-polling loop.
frozen_decisions: OOOI events: reuse the existing flight state machine (flightManager.ts) transitions — pushback/taxi-out as OUT, takeoff as OFF, landing as ON, arrival at gate/parking as IN — to emit one message per event with a timestamp, rather than adding new state detection logic.

Enroute position reports: at a configurable interval (e.g. every N minutes or every leg waypoint crossed, reusing legMatcher.ts's notion of progress along the route), emit a downlink message with current position, altitude, and ETA to next fix/destination if a route is attached.
No attached route -> OOOI-only reporting; skip position reports rather than failing.
Reports write into the shared ACARS message table as downlink, category position-report / oooi.
Reporting interval is configurable (env var or setting), with a sane default, since track density already varies by sim/agent polling rate.
Should not add new position-polling logic - piggyback on the track ingestion path that already exists for the live map/traffic feature.
Keep report volume bounded on long-haul flights; an interval-based or waypoint-based cadence, not per-tick.
Acceptance 1: Each OOOI transition produces exactly one message, timestamped to the existing state-transition event (no duplicate or missing events across a normal flight).
Acceptance 2: A flight with an attached route produces at least one position report between OFF and ON, on the configured interval.
Acceptance 3: A flight without an attached route produces OOOI messages only, with no errors from the missing route.
Acceptance 4: Reports are visible in the same per-flight thread as other ACARS messages.
KNOWN_ACARS_CATEGORIES already has 'oooi' and 'position-report' - use them as-is, no new category, no schema migration expected.
Reuse insertAcarsMessageOnce + a dedup key per OOOI event/report tick, matching the existing dispatch/loadsheet pattern, so re-delivery or a duplicate frame can never double-file a message.
Never touch the user's live server or flights.db - scratch copies, other ports.
Tier 3, full loop, with a Design step before implementation; Ship is skipped (no build/packaging/deploy/CI/env-secrets surface touched).
sequencing_rationale: The OOOI-to-transition mapping (which FlightManager method each of OUT/OFF/ON/IN fires from, and whether a leg-less-flight edge case backfills or skips OUT) and the position-report cadence/ETA formula are not determined by existing code per the intake's own reading notes - this is the contract the run introduces, so Design must freeze it before any implementation task, the same way acars_message_center's schema was frozen before PDC/WX were built on it.

Both OOOI emission and position-report emission wire into the same file, src/flightManager.ts (OOOI into its existing transition methods - enterGround/startFlight/endFlight/closeGroundSessionAndReturnToIdle - and position reports into its onFrame -> recordPoint -> writePoint chain), and both need new pure builder functions in the same file, src/acars.ts. Per the 'two edits to the same file are one task' rule, these ship as a single backend_sr implementation task rather than two tasks that could never actually run in parallel and would only re-read the same context cold twice.

No new route, query or client change is needed: insertAcarsMessageOnce already generalises to any category/dedup_key, listAcarsMessagesForFlight() already unions a flight's own rows with its linked planned leg's rows so a leg-scoped OOOI message surfaces in the flight thread once linked, and the client (client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx, client/src/index.css) already renders 'oooi' and 'position-report' badges generically since KNOWN_ACARS_CATEGORIES shipped with both already listed. This keeps the run to one phase, backend-only.

One phase is enough because the design task and the single implementation task together ship the whole user-visible feature (both OOOI and position reports appear in the ACARS thread) in one step; splitting into more phases would only add a reviewer gate with nothing shippable in between.

The phase ends in a reviewer task per the standing rule, verifying both that the frozen design was followed and that all four story acceptance criteria hold, since this is the only implementation task and there is no earlier phase's review to lean on.

phases.name: OOOI events and position reports in the ACARS thread
phases.ships: Every flight now files OUT/OFF/ON/IN messages into its ACARS thread at the right moments, and a flight with an attached route also files periodic position reports (position, altitude, ETA) between OFF and ON at a configurable interval; a flight with no attached route still gets clean OOOI-only reporting.

tasks.title: Freeze the OOOI-to-transition mapping and the position-report cadence/ETA contract
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-16-acars-position-reports/design.md that resolves everything the intake flags as undetermined by existing code: exactly which FlightManager method/event each of OUT, OFF, ON, IN fires from (FlightManager's state machine is IDLE -> GROUND -> FLYING -> IDLE; startFlight() and endFlight() are the only two existing transitions that correspond to leaving/touching the ground - OUT and IN have no distinct instrumentation today and must be mapped onto enterGround()/closeGroundSessionAndReturnToIdle() or approximated onto the same instant as OFF/ON, a real decision); the dedup_key format and label/body text for all four OOOI events and for position reports, following the dispatchDedupKey/loadsheetRequestDedupKey precedent (src/acars.ts) and the <category>:<scope>:<id> shape, extended to something that also prevents a periodic position report from double-filing within one interval window; whether each event files with flight_id, planned_leg_id, or both, given that a ground-session OUT may have no flights row yet; the exact point inside onFrame -> recordPoint -> writePoint (src/flightManager.ts) where the position-report interval check runs, confirming it adds no new timer/polling loop; the interval's config knob - name, unit, default, and whether it follows the TRAFFIC_ENABLED precedent of a direct process.env read (src/config.ts's own header comment restricts AppConfig/ENV_VARS to security-relevant settings, so a plain interval likely does not belong there - confirm this explicitly rather than leaving it to the implementer); the ETA formula (groundspeed-based, from getPlannedLegStatus()'s remainingDistanceNm and the frame's groundSpeedKnots, or a new field getPlannedLegStatus() must return) and its behaviour at zero/near-zero groundspeed; and the exact skip condition (plannedLegCache === null) for 'no route attached', confirming zero position-report messages and zero thrown errors on that path. Read src/flightManager.ts, src/acars.ts, src/db/acarsMessages.ts, src/routes/plannedLegs.ts (dispatch/loadsheet dedup-key wiring), src/routes/acars.ts, src/legMatcher.ts, src/config.ts and src/types.ts (PlannedLegLiveStatus, AcarsCategory, CreateAcarsMessage) before writing it - do not re-derive facts already stated in intake.md, cite them.
acceptance_criteria: design.md section 1 states, for each of OUT, OFF, ON, IN, the exact FlightManager method/event it fires from, and states explicitly what happens when a flight reaches FLYING with no antecedent GROUND state in this session (OUT skipped, or backfilled some other way) - a stated choice, not left ambiguous.

design.md section 1 states which of the four events file with flight_id and which (if any, because no flights row exists yet) file with planned_leg_id only, and states whether a leg-scoped OOOI message is ever reconciled to a flight_id once one exists, or is left relying on listAcarsMessagesForFlight()'s existing join on the flight's own planned_leg_id.

design.md section 2 defines the dedup_key format, label and body text for each of the four OOOI events and for a position report, in the <category>:<scope>:<id> style of dispatchDedupKey/loadsheetRequestDedupKey (src/acars.ts:140-148), and the position-report key specifically prevents two reports from the same interval window from ever double-filing.

design.md section 3 states exactly where inside onFrame -> recordPoint -> writePoint (src/flightManager.ts) the position-report interval check runs, and confirms in prose that it adds no new setInterval/setTimeout/polling loop - it only ever fires on a frame that already reached that path.

design.md section 3 also names the config knob (env var name, unit, default value) and states explicitly whether it is read directly where consumed (TRAFFIC_ENABLED precedent) or added to AppConfig/ENV_VARS in src/config.ts, with a one-line reason tied to that module's own security-relevant-only header comment.

design.md section 4 gives the exact ETA formula and its unit, states which existing field(s) (getPlannedLegStatus()'s remainingDistanceNm, the frame's groundSpeedKnots) it is built from or exactly what new field getPlannedLegStatus() must additionally return, and states the value at zero or near-zero groundspeed (e.g. null/omitted, never Infinity or a divide-by-zero).

design.md section 5 states the skip condition for 'no route attached' (plannedLegCache === null) and confirms it produces zero position-report messages and no thrown exception or console.error on that path.

design.md section 6 names the new pure functions T-002 adds to src/acars.ts, with parameter and return types, for the OOOI dedup-keys/bodies and the position-report dedup-key/body, in the style of buildDispatchReleaseBody/dispatchDedupKey, so T-002 can write Vitest coverage test-first against a frozen signature.

tasks.title: Emit OOOI events and periodic position reports from FlightManager, per the frozen design
tasks.goal: Implement exactly the contract frozen in .claude/runs/2026-09-16-acars-position-reports/design.md (all sections) - no re-deriving the OOOI mapping or the cadence/ETA formula from scratch. Add the pure builder functions design.md section 6 names to src/acars.ts (dedup keys, labels, bodies for the four OOOI events and for a position report), then wire them into src/flightManager.ts at the exact call sites design.md section 1 and 3 name, using insertAcarsMessageOnce (already imported from './db' in this codebase's barrel - src/db.ts re-exports src/db/acarsMessages.ts, so no new import path is needed) for every write. Add the config knob per design.md section 3 exactly as specified (env var name, default, read location). Give every new pure function in src/acars.ts Vitest coverage in tests/acars.test.ts (mirroring the existing buildDispatchReleaseBody/dispatchDedupKey style tests), and give the FlightManager wiring Vitest coverage by driving FlightManager.onFrame() through full scenarios (mirroring tests/flightManager.state.test.ts and tests/flightManager.ground.test.ts's pattern of vi.mock('../src/db', ...) against tests/helpers/index.ts's dbMock) in a new file, tests/flightManager.acars.test.ts - add insertAcarsMessageOnce (and any other new src/db.ts export FlightManager now calls) to dbMock and its installDbMockDefaults()/resetMocks() in tests/helpers/index.ts, since that file is this run's only owner for this change. Do not add a new route, a new query in src/db/acarsMessages.ts, or any client-side change - none is needed (KNOWN_ACARS_CATEGORIES, the client's badge CSS and AcarsMessages.tsx already know 'oooi'/'position-report', and listAcarsMessagesForFlight already unions a flight's own rows with its linked planned leg's).
acceptance_criteria: npm run build (npx tsc) succeeds with no new type errors.

npm test passes, including the new tests/acars.test.ts coverage for every new builder/dedup-key function added to src/acars.ts (values in, values out - no clock, no database, per that file's own header convention).

AC1: a Vitest scenario in tests/flightManager.acars.test.ts drives FlightManager.onFrame() through a full OUT->OFF->ON->IN cycle (ground debounce, airborne debounce, landed debounce, per tests/flightManager.state.test.ts's existing frame-sequence pattern) and asserts the dbMock.insertAcarsMessageOnce mock (or equivalent) was called exactly once per OOOI event, each with the dedup_key design.md section 2 specifies and a timestamp matching the transition frame, with zero duplicate calls when the same frame sequence around one transition is replayed (simulating an agent retry).

AC2: a Vitest scenario with a plannedLegCache attached (via tests/helpers/index.ts's makePlannedLegWithChildren, following the linking path flightManager.state/ground tests already use) and a FLYING period longer than the configured interval produces at least one category:'position-report' insertAcarsMessageOnce call strictly between the OFF-equivalent and ON-equivalent transitions, per npm test.

AC3: a Vitest scenario with no plannedLegCache attached (the flight never links to a planned leg) runs the same full flight through onFrame() and asserts only category:'oooi' messages are ever filed - zero 'position-report' calls - and that onFrame() throws nothing and logs no console.error for the missing route, per npm test.

AC4: the OOOI and position-report calls built in T-002 pass either flight_id or planned_leg_id exactly as design.md section 1 specifies; a Vitest test (in tests/db/acarsMessages.test.ts if that file needs no change, or asserted at the flightManager.acars.test.ts mock-call level if it does) confirms the identifiers used are what listAcarsMessagesForFlight()'s existing WHERE flight_id = ? OR planned_leg_id = (flight's own planned_leg_id) clause (src/db/acarsMessages.ts) would actually match - i.e. the messages are provably reachable from the flight's own thread, not just written to the table.
The config knob is read exactly where and how design.md section 3 specifies (confirm by reading the diff against that section), with the stated default value when unset.

tasks.title: Review phase 1: OOOI events and position reports
tasks.goal: Re-run the evidence, not just read the diff. Confirm the implementation in src/acars.ts and src/flightManager.ts matches every decision frozen in .claude/runs/2026-09-16-acars-position-reports/design.md (no silent re-derivation of the OOOI mapping or cadence/ETA formula), and independently verify all four story acceptance criteria (quoted in T-002's goal and this run's frozen_decisions) by actually running npm test and npm run build under Node 20 (per .claude/ENVIRONMENT.md), not by trusting T-002's report. Check specifically: that no new position-polling loop was added (grep for setInterval/setTimeout in the diff to src/flightManager.ts - there should be none new); that every OOOI/position-report write goes through insertAcarsMessageOnce with a dedup_key, never insertAcarsMessage; that the no-route path truly produces zero position-report messages and zero errors; and that tests/helpers/index.ts's dbMock update is consistent with every new src/db.ts export FlightManager now calls.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict is 'approve' or 'request_changes' with concrete file:line findings for each requested change.
npm test and npm run build (npx tsc) were both actually run under Node 20 (nvm use 20) and their output is quoted or summarized in the review, not merely asserted.

Each of the four story acceptance criteria (OOOI exactly-once-per-transition, at-least-one position report on a routed flight, OOOI-only with no errors on an unrouted flight, visibility in the flight's own ACARS thread) is checked off individually against either an existing test or a manual scratch-server check, not waved through as a group.
Confirms no client-side file, no new route, and no new src/db/acarsMessages.ts query were touched, since design established none was needed - flags it if T-002 added any.
